pr_body:
# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/5009

## What does this PR do?
- Force every analytics to go through a trait that forces you to handle aggregation correcty
- Put the code to retrieve the `user-agent`, `timestamp` and `requests.total_received` in common between all aggregates, so there is no mistake
- Get rids of all the different channel for each kind of event in favor of an any map
- Ensure that we never [send empty event ever again](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5001)
- Merge all the sub-settings route into a global « Settings Updated » event.
- Fix: When using one of the three following feature, we were not sending any analytics IF they were set from the global route
  - /non-separator-tokens
  - /separator-tokens
  - /dictionary
pr_comments:
I think I messed up the settings. When I started using the or instead of the map_or stuff, I should have swapped the order of the self and other field to select the new one instead of the old one.

+ I want to rename the argument of the aggregate function trait to call it "new" instead of "other" so it's clearer which version is new and old
I don’t think we need to integrate the helper function into the trait, we can simply specialize it at compile time and get a ptr to it without putting it in the trait

issue_context.title: Revamp the analytics
issue_context.body:

- [x] Send all the experimental features through the `info` identify event
- [x] For all settings, return the last value OR null if it wasn’t modified
- [x] Aggregate everything
- [x] Store the timestamp of **the first event** and set it correctly
- [x] Store the user-agent of **every requests** and set it correctly
- [x] Add a `requests.total_received` to all the events
- [x] Remove the experimental feature seen
